answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require a 100-token bond locked for 30 days and three independent audits before an identity gains voting weight. Each additional identity raises the bond by 25% and adds one audit round, making collusion increasingly expensive. Random peers verify signed task receipts; failure slashes the bond and freezes rewards. A copper trail of verified work can cross a gale of coordinated claims and move honest agents up the governance ridge.
